authoring_note: Original content informed by the public framework structure and role-profile intent. No Jisc descriptor text is reproduced or closely paraphrased.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, keeps essential digital tasks moving but still relies on prompts, familiar routines or local help when work becomes less predictable.
observable_practices: Uses VLE module spaces for routine teaching, assessment and student support when a known example or clear instructions are available.
Keeps digital assessment workflows moving with some structure, but consistency drops when the task becomes unfamiliar or time-pressured.
Can recover from minor issues in live teaching platforms through search, help or local support, although interruptions still slow progress.
evidence_examples: Examples showing routine use of VLE module spaces for predictable tasks.
A simple file, checklist or message trail in digital assessment workflows that shows work can be completed, albeit with some friction.
A support request, self-note or reflection describing how an issue in live teaching platforms was resolved.

common_misconceptions.claim: Owning or accessing many apps means the basics are secure.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Breadth of access can hide fragile workflow habits and version confusion.

common_misconceptions.claim: Getting through the task once shows the process is reliable.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: One-off success does not show independent, repeatable practice.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, uses core tools independently, chooses sensible workflows and solves common issues without much interruption.
observable_practices: Uses VLE module spaces independently and chooses sensible settings or features for the job rather than relying on default habits.
Organises digital assessment workflows so that current materials, deadlines and permissions are easier for other people to follow.
Troubleshoots common problems in live teaching platforms and makes practical choices that reduce avoidable friction.
evidence_examples: A clean, consistently used setup in VLE module spaces that other people can navigate without extra explanation.
A short process note, template or annotated example from digital assessment workflows showing independent workflow choices.
A troubleshooting example from live teaching platforms where the person diagnosed and fixed a common problem.

common_misconceptions.claim: Being quick personally is the same as having a good workflow.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: A strong personal workaround may still be opaque or awkward for others.

common_misconceptions.claim: A preferred tool is automatically the right choice everywhere.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Fit depends on context, interoperability, support and inclusion.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, optimises workflows, judges tool choices critically and improves practice for other people as well as for themselves.
observable_practices: Improves VLE module spaces so that reliability, accessibility or efficiency increase for a wider group, not just for personal use.
Reviews digital assessment workflows critically, removing duplication and simplifying the workflow where needed.
Makes well-judged decisions about live teaching platforms with attention to interoperability, support burden, inclusion and risk.
evidence_examples: A redesigned or simplified approach to VLE module spaces adopted by others or endorsed locally.
Before-and-after evidence from digital assessment workflows showing improved reliability, accessibility or efficiency.
A comparison or rationale for choices in live teaching platforms that weighs fit, risk, support and interoperability.

common_misconceptions.claim: Proficiency means always adopting the newest or most advanced platform.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Judgment and simplification often matter more than feature depth.

common_misconceptions.claim: If a process works for experts it should work for everyone.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Sustainable improvement must account for different users, needs and support conditions.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, adapts existing materials or familiar methods to meet immediate needs, but design choices are still mostly guided by examples rather than by clear intent.
observable_practices: Adapts existing learning activities and resources for immediate use, but most choices still follow familiar patterns rather than an explicit design rationale.
Uses feedback or assessment designs to solve a local problem once the route is reasonably clear.
Experiments with accessible learning materials in a limited way, though evaluation is still mainly about whether something worked at all.
evidence_examples: An adapted version of learning activities and resources based on an existing model.
A local workaround using feedback or assessment designs that addresses an immediate need.
A brief note on what was changed in accessible learning materials, even if evaluation is still limited.

common_misconceptions.claim: Changing the look of something counts as innovation.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Surface polish does not by itself improve fitness for purpose.

common_misconceptions.claim: Trying a new tool is enough evidence of creative capability.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Capability lies in the problem solved and the design decisions made.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, creates purposeful outputs or workflow changes that fit the user need, the task and the context.
observable_practices: Designs learning activities and resources around the need, the users and the context rather than around the tool alone.
Uses feedback or assessment designs to remove repeated effort or improve clarity, consistency or accessibility.
Tests and refines accessible learning materials enough to show that the change is genuinely useful.
evidence_examples: A purposeful design in learning activities and resources with visible choices about structure, format or accessibility.
Evidence that feedback or assessment designs reduced repeated effort or improved the user experience.
Feedback or review notes showing that accessible learning materials was refined after real use.

common_misconceptions.claim: A useful one-off output is automatically reusable.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Reusability usually needs documentation, testing and adaptation for others.

common_misconceptions.claim: More interactivity always means better design.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Good design serves the need; extra features can add friction.

entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, designs reusable, evaluative and innovative solutions that improve practice beyond the immediate task.
observable_practices: Creates learning activities and resources that other people can reuse, adapt or scale with minimal extra explanation.
Treats feedback or assessment designs as part of an improvement cycle, with feedback and evidence informing later iterations.
Uses accessible learning materials to support original, well-scoped innovation rather than novelty for its own sake.

Evidence from feedback or assessment designs showing evaluation, iteration and decisions about scale or adaptation.

common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Many proficient innovations are focused, evidence-led and appropriately scoped.

common_misconceptions.claim: Once a digital solution works, evaluation can stop.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Proficient practice keeps learning from use, context change and feedback.

entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, learns reactively when a new need appears and often stops once the immediate task is complete.
observable_practices: Uses CPD resources on digital pedagogy when a new need arises, but development activity is still mostly reactive and short-term.
Tries out ideas from teaching experiments in isolated moments without always checking what changed in practice.
Joins peer review or scholarship exchanges when prompted or when confidence is low, though follow-through may be limited once the pressure passes.
evidence_examples: Completion of CPD resources on digital pedagogy linked to an immediate need.

common_misconceptions.claim: Only formal courses count as digital development.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Practice, peer exchange and experimentation also matter.

Uses teaching experiments to make practice visible, reflective and evidence-informed at group level.

Facilitated use of teaching experiments with evidence that confidence or practice shifted across a group.

common_misconceptions.claim: Attendance proves that development has happened.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Proficient development looks for transfer into real practice.

entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, finds usable sources or data for immediate tasks, but evaluation of quality, limitations and relevance is still inconsistent.
observable_practices: Uses learning analytics or grade data to locate material for immediate tasks, but source quality checks are still inconsistent.
Reads education research or guidance with some care, though assumptions, gaps or definitions can still be missed.
Draws on media and source sets for teaching to support decisions, but confidence is sometimes based more on convenience than on evidence strength.

A worked example using education research or guidance with some attention to meaning, though not all assumptions are checked.
A note or draft using media and source sets for teaching that shows a plausible but still limited evidence base.

common_misconceptions.claim: A source is reliable if it appears high in search results or looks professional.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Presentation and ranking do not guarantee trustworthiness or fit.

common_misconceptions.claim: Numbers speak for themselves.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Data always depends on definitions, omissions, context and interpretation.

entries.capability_statement: In the context of a higher education teacher designing, teaching and assessing learning, judges source quality, data definitions and relevance deliberately, then uses evidence with care.
observable_practices: Uses learning analytics or grade data deliberately to compare relevance, credibility and fit for purpose.
Interprets education research or guidance with attention to definitions, missing information, timeframe and context.
Uses media and source sets for teaching to make reasoned judgments and can explain the limits of the evidence.

An annotated interpretation of education research or guidance that explains caveats, definitions or missing data.

common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Critical literacy often requires weighing imperfect evidence, not just discarding it.

common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Visual clarity can conceal weak measures, missing data or poor alignment with the question.
